criteria.rationale: The CLI-to-runtime boundary (pose runtime run, hosted handler and worktreeruntime endpoint) and the CLI/MCP shared operation boundary are covered by sealed integration evidence (optional-worktree-runtime, resident-cache, runtime-qos and common-domain-and-cli-mcp-handoff integration all pass).

Each milestone exit gate (B32, B31, B33, B35) has a sealed passing integration check (governance-operation-performance, common-domain-and-cli-mcp-handoff, bounded-isolated-graph-caches, optional-worktree-runtime, resident-cache and runtime-qos). The B35 departures (no CPU quota or affinity, no per-command limits, Windows standalone) are declared in ADR lines 296-311 and the roadmap's Estado paragraph.

The user-facing path (start the runtime, run a hosted check through pose runtime run, fall back to standalone) is exercised by the sealed optional-worktree-runtime integration check. The hosted handler (runtime_host.go:82-166) refuses an unhosted command or a mismatched environment before running anything.

All six member specs and the two engine specs are status done. The implementer states that each milestone has an approved independent review; per the brief I judged the roadmap, not the review records, which are absent from this checkout.

The stated outcome is coherent CLI/MCP operations, controlled cost per producer, bounded reuse, and an optional runtime only after qualification. It is supported by sealed common-domain, operation-performance, bounded-cache and runtime checks. The round-1 blocker on memo-key staleness is fixed (R1-F1).

POSE.md, its pt-BR locale and the scaffold dist copies change together under a passing parity check. Six unreleased changelog entries exist, one per member spec. The ADR status is consistent; only low documentation drift remains (N1, N2).
No medium or high risk remains. Open items are low follow-ups (R1-F2, N1, N2), and the four not-delivered capabilities each have a draft spec of their own.
